summary: In this excerpt from Book 4, a girl named Valentine is stopped by a soldier named Withnail near her block of flats. Unable to share a language, they communicate through a few phrases and then share butter-balls, which calms the tense standoff. Valentine asks him to let her go to save her family, and after a squeeze of his hand he releases her arm, though she worries she may die that afternoon if she cannot return to her own trenches.
one_line: Valentine, a girl facing a gun-wielding soldier named Withnail, shares butter-balls with him and persuades him to let her go.
key_facts: Valentine knows a few words of the other side's language, learned from a cine across from her block of flats.
The soldier says "Friend!" to Valentine and then switches to two other languages she does not recognize or only partly knows.
Valentine's only Hindi phrase is "Love Love Love I'm in Love", the chorus of Hindi movie songs.
The soldier's handgun is described as a soft, floppy handgun like a length of rope.
Valentine reasons that if she were a suicide bomber, the soldier would already be dead, which makes her feel a little better about the war.
Valentine offers the soldier butter-balls from her pocket, and they eat alternately, one bite each, until the butter-ball is gone.
The soldier introduces himself as "Withnail" and shakes Valentine's hand after she says "Pleased to make your acquaintance, Withnail".
Valentine tells Withnail, "To save my family", and says she is on a mission for his side anyway.
Withnail slowly releases Valentine's arm after she squeezes his hand and asks him to let her go.
Valentine has never kissed a boy and believes she will be dead in four days and a little more.
Valentine fears she may be dead that afternoon if she cannot get back into her own trenches.
